title: Reading the night sky
question: How did people turn watching the night sky into a science?
hook: Long before telescopes, people noticed that the sky repeats itself, and that single habit built a whole science.
idea: Astronomy grew from careful sky-watching into a science that explains everything beyond Earth's atmosphere.

beats.prompt: Scribes in Babylon record every lunar eclipse for generations and compare their notes. What do they find?

choices.label: Eclipses come in a repeating cycle that can be counted in months
Eclipses strike at random, so no pattern can ever be found
choices.feedback: It looks random from one night to the next, but the long record shows a pattern.

choices.label: Eclipses happen only in one season of the year
choices.feedback: A season is an easy guess, but the repeat is counted in months, not seasons.

choices.label: Eclipses follow the farming calendar exactly
choices.feedback: Calendars were built from the sky, but the eclipse repeat is its own cycle.

beats.explain: The Babylonians discovered that lunar eclipses recurred in the saros cycle of 223 synodic months, part of the start of mathematical and scientific astronomy.

beats.prompt: Put these developments in order, earliest first.
items: Heracleides Ponticus proposes that the Earth rotates on its own axis
Aristarchus of Samos proposes that the Earth and planets go around the Sun
Mechanical astronomical clocks appear in Europe
beats.explain: These run from the 4th century BC, to the 3rd century BC, to the 2nd century BC, to the 14th century.

beats.prompt: Match each astronomer or people to what they are known for.
pairs: Improved methods for calculating planetary motions and eclipses
beats.explain: Each of them added a tool, a record, or a calculation method that later astronomers could build on.

beats.prompt: Sort each item into the group astronomy uses for it.
beats.explain: Planets, comets, and galaxies are objects of interest, while supernova explosions, gamma ray bursts, and quasars are phenomena.
